question: Which prime-three Kervaire classes survive the homotopy calculation?
idea: A spectral sequence is a staged calculation in which candidate classes may disappear along the way. The manuscript claims exactly three of the specified standard prime-three Kervaire candidates survive, at indices zero, two and three. Each surviving detection class contains an element of exact additive order three.
why: The study of properties of shapes preserved by continuous stretching, such as connectedness and holes.

glossary.meaning: A prime is a whole number greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself.
Spectral questions concern values, such as eigenvalues, associated with an operator or system.

exactClaim: Resolves the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: exactly the standard classes with indices 0, 2, and 3 survive in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence, in stems 10, 106, and 322. Each surviving detection coset contains an element of exact additive order three.
